papers.title: Biomechanical Evaluation of Different Posterior Mandibular Implant Configurations Under Bruxism: An FEA Study
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the biomechanical performance of different abutment types, superstructure materials, prosthetic designs, and loading conditions in the implant-supported rehabilitation of three consecutive missing teeth in the mandibular posterior region using three-dimensional finite element analysis (3D-FEA). Twenty FEA models were constructed, simulating two-implant (pontic, mesial, and distal cantilever) and three-implant (splinted and unsplinted) configurations using multi-unit and Ti-base abutments composed of titanium alloy (Grade 5, Ti-6Al-4V), with monolithic zirconia and zirconia-supported feldspathic porcelain superstructures. Functional and parafunctional (bruxism) vertical and oblique loads were applied to analyze von Mises stresses in the components and principal stresses in the peri-implant bone. The results indicated that two-implant models generated higher stress concentrations than three-implant models, and unsplinted or cantilevered designs produced elevated stresses compared to splinted or pontic designs. Ti-base abutments resulted in greater stress accumulation in the connection complex compared to multi-unit systems. Under vertical and oblique parafunctional forces, stress values on the abutments in distal cantilever models—particularly in unsplinted Ti-base designs under oblique loading—exceeded the yield strength of the Ti-6Al-4V alloy (890 MPa), indicating a substantial risk of plastic deformation. To optimize biomechanical stability, three-implant-supported, splinted designs utilizing Multi-unit abutments should be prioritized. Avoiding distal cantilevers and unsplinted designs is critical in patients with bruxism to minimize the risk of mechanical failure in the Ti-6Al-4V components.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文为牙科种植体配置的有限元分析，未涉及增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的力学或疲劳性能，与用户关注方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V; it is a finite element study of dental implant prosthetic configurations using conventionally fabricated Ti-6Al-4V components, with no mechanical or fatigue characterization of AM material.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估不同种植体配置在磨牙症下的生物力学性能，以避免机械失效。
summary_zh.method: 建立20个三维有限元模型，比较两种植体与三种植体、不同基台和修复体设计在功能及副功能载荷下的应力。
summary_zh.result: 三种植体夹板式设计应力最低，悬臂和非夹板式设计风险高，部分Ti-6Al-4V基台应力超过屈服强度。
summary_zh.validation: 仅采用有限元模拟，无实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: The study aimed to evaluate the biomechanical performance of various implant-supported configurations for three missing posterior mandibular teeth under functional and parafunctional loads.
summary_en.method: Twenty 3D finite element models were developed to compare two- and three-implant designs with different abutment systems, superstructure materials, and loading conditions, assessing von Mises and principal stresses.
summary_en.result: Three-implant splinted designs with multi-unit abutments showed lower stress concentrations, while distal cantilever and unsplinted Ti-base abutments under oblique parafunctional loading exceeded the Ti-6Al-4V yield strength, indicating plastic deformation risk.
summary_en.validation: The study is purely computational, relying on finite element analysis without experimental or clinical validation.
